borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
description: Conversion of the existing dwelling into three flats (2x 1bed and 1x 3bed) including the construction of a part two storey part single storey rear extension, a part two storey part single storey side extension, a single storey front extension and a rear L-Shaped dormer extension including 6 roof lights to the front and a Juliette balcony
decision_conditions: <p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The proposed development fails to demonstrate that the proposal would not exacerbate existing parking stress within the area given&nbsp;</span><span style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 11pt;">would result in the loss of 1x on-street parking space to create a larger dropped kerb ensure each flat would have individual access to 1x off-street car parking space.</span><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">&nbsp;As such, it fails to comply with the following policies which seek to ensure proposals show how car parking will be designed and managed and to take into consideration on-street parking availability and existing and planned public transport provision: National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024) Policies T1, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021) Policy DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The proposed two-storey side extension, by reason of its design, scale and siting, would disrupt the symmetry across the host semi-detached pair would result in an overdevelopment of the site when combined with the other proposed extensions, thus would be at odds with the character and appearance of the host dwelling and surrounding area.&nbsp;</span></span><span style="font-size: 11pt; text-align: justify;">n. As such, the proposed development is contrary to:</span></p><ul><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December 2024);</span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">Policies D1, D4, D5 and D6 of the London Plan (March 2021); </span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">Policies DMD1, DMD5 and SP2 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham's Local Plan (September 2024); and</span></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:11pt">The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)</span></li></ul>

<p><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The proposal would result in the loss of a high-quality family dwellinghouse, the need for which is clearly demonstrated in the development plan and evidence base. Whilst the proposal would provide a family-sized additional unit, this is not considered to outweigh the harm caused through this loss as the proposed flats would be of a lesser quality than the existing dwellinghouse thus would </span></span><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">adversely impact the quality of the existing accommodation for future occupants.</span></span><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">&nbsp;</span></span><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">&nbsp;</span><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">As such, the proposal is considered to have a detrimental impact on the borough's supply of family housing and is contrary to the following policies: - National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)- Policies D6, D14 and T4 of the London Plan (March 2021)- Policies SP3, SP8, DMD1, DMT1, DMH5 and DMSI3 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)</span></p>
